title: Make a commit in the sandbox
task: Change a file and commit it. The goals below are checked against the repository itself, not against what you typed.

title: Delete a branch without losing the work
task: This repo already had a branch deleted — experiment is gone. Prove the commits survived it, and put a branch back on them.

title: Walk from the commit to the file
task: Using only cat-file and rev-parse, get from HEAD to the contents of notes/plan.md — then prove you found the right blob by committing its id into a file called found.txt.

title: Commit without using git commit
task: Add a file hi.py containing print('hi') to main, using only hash-object, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree and update-ref. git commit is off-limits.

title: Put an object in the database by hand
task: Write a blob containing the exact text hello world (with a trailing newline) into the object database — without staging or committing anything.

title: Create and move a branch with plumbing only
task: Without using git branch, checkout, switch or reset: create a branch spike pointing three commits back, then make HEAD point at it.

title: Name four commits four different ways
task: Write a file answers.txt with four lines, each the full id of: (1) the commit two back from main, (2) the tip of feature, (3) the commit whose message mentions the README, (4) the tree of main. Commit it.

title: Put HEAD, the index and the worktree in three different states
task: Get count.py into the state where HEAD, the index and the working tree all hold different content — then commit only what's in the index, and confirm your worktree edit survived.

title: Amend a commit, then undo the amend
task: Amend the last commit so its subject is Report the longest line as well — then put the original commit back exactly as it was, using the reflog.

title: Backport the hotfix, traceably
task: Get the hotfix commit onto main so the message records where it came from — and leave the hotfix branch exactly where it is.

title: Turn three WIP commits into one clean commit
task: Run git rebase -i HEAD~3 and squash the three commits into a single commit whose subject is Add the report module. The files must not change.

title: Move one commit and leave the rest behind
task: Get only feature's newest commit (“Sort the report output”) onto main, leaving the older “Start the report module” commit out of the branch entirely.

title: Do it both ways and keep the evidence
task: First merge main into feature. Then undo that and rebase instead — so the branch ends up rebased, and the reflog shows you tried both.

title: Destroy a branch, then bring it back
task: Delete feature/report outright, then recreate its exact tip as a branch called rescued — using the reflog rather than remembering the id.

title: Collapse three commits with reset --soft
task: The three WIP commits on feature/report should be one commit called Add the report module — and the files must come out identical. Do it with reset, not rebase.

title: Read a divergence before you fix it
task: Work out exactly how your branch and origin/main have diverged, then integrate the remote's commit without force-pushing — leaving both sides' work in place.

title: Let autosquash place two marked commits
task: Fold the fixup! and squash! commits into the commits they name, leaving three clean commits and no marker subjects — with all the content intact.

title: Find the commit that broke the tokenizer
task: Twelve commits; one introduced text.split(" ") where text.split() belongs. Bisect until git names it, then git bisect reset and record the culprit's id (or its subject) in culprit.txt.

title: Find where the reporting code really came from
task: The show_counts function lives in report.py, but it wasn't written there. Find the commit that actually introduced those lines, and record its subject in a file called origin.txt.

title: Rescue lost work with fsck alone
task: Find the stranded commits with fsck and put a branch called recovered on the newest one — the tip of the lost chain, not one of its ancestors.

title: Work out how long the password was exposed
task: The string hunter2 was committed and later removed. Find both commits and record, in incident.txt, the subjects of the commit that introduced it and the commit that removed it — one per line, introduced first.

title: Reconstruct what happened to this repository
task: Using only the reflog, work out the id the deleted experiment branch pointed at when it was last committed to, and write it into found.txt.

title: Get a lease refused, then earn it
task: First try to push, and try again with --force-with-lease — both should be refused. Then fetch, integrate the remote's commit, and push successfully without ever using plain --force.

title: Write a pre-commit hook that refuses bad commits
task: Write .git/hooks/pre-commit so that committing anything containing the text TODO is refused. Then prove it: try a commit that should fail, and make one that succeeds.

title: Hit a conflict, then resolve it deliberately
task: Merge tune-cache into main. It will conflict on config.ini. Resolve it so the file ends up with cache = 256 — neither side's value — and commit the merge.

title: Push your branch to the remote under a different name
task: Publish your local main to the remote as a branch called review/main, without touching the remote's own main. Then delete it again with a refspec.

title: Stash everything, prove it's a commit, bring it back
task: Shelve all of it — including the untracked scratch.txt — leaving the worktree clean. Then restore it, so you end up back where you started with the stash gone.

title: Read a submodule as data
task: Find the commit id this repository pins for vendor/parser, and write it into pinned.txt. Nothing needs committing.

title: Build the .git/worktrees layout by hand
task: Create the metadata a linked worktree for feature would have: a directory .git/worktrees/review/ containing a HEAD that points at refs/heads/feature, and a commondir file containing ../...

title: Drill 1 — the branch that isn't there any more
task: Someone deleted the experiment branch. Two commits of work went with it. Get them back on a branch called experiment again — same name, same tip.

title: Drill 2 — the reset that went too far
task: Run git reset --hard HEAD~4 — then put main back where it was, with all five commits and the files intact.

title: Drill 3 — the commit on the wrong branch
task: Commit something on main that belonged on feature — add a line to report.py and commit it as Add a docstring. Then move that commit to feature and leave main as it was.

title: Drill 4 — nine commits, one reviewable change
task: This branch has five commits, two of which are corrections marked fixup! and squash!. Turn it into three clean commits with no marker subjects, without changing any file.

title: Linear history
task: Five commits on one branch. Nothing to achieve — break it however you like.

title: Diverged branches
task: main, feature and hotfix, all pointing at different places.

title: With a remote
task: origin has a commit you don't. Try pushing, and see what it takes to get it through.

title: Build a note with plumbing
task: Attach a note to the tip commit the way git notes would: a blob containing Reviewed by Priya, at a path named after the commit's full id, in a tree, in a commit, pointed at by refs/notes/commits.

title: Count what a commit actually costs
task: Note how many objects this repository has, then make one commit that changes one line of one file, and work out how many new objects appeared. Write the number into cost.txt.
